content.title: About
content.content: Wheat biscuit is a baked product made from wheat flour, sugar, butter, and often additives such as leavening agents, vanilla, or spices. It has a crisp or soft texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and is commonly enjoyed as a light snack or accompaniment to tea and coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat biscuits originated in Europe in the 19th century and quickly became popular due to their simple preparation.
There are many variations: with raisins, nuts, chocolate, or spices.
Traditionally biscuits are baked as round or square pieces, but modern shapes can be any geometry.
Biscuits are often used as a base for dessert layers, such as in tiramisu.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat biscuits provide quick‑acting carbs that rapidly replenish energy.

items.title: Contains some fiber
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, biscuits can contribute to digestive health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Biscuits contain iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, supporting various bodily functions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat biscuits contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some recipes use partially hydrogenated oils, which contain trans fats harmful to heart health.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Biscuits may contain nuts, eggs, or dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Biscuits can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with tea, coffee, or milk, used in dessert layers, crumbled into yogurt or ice cream. For a healthier option, choose whole‑grain biscuits without added sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store biscuits in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth and maintain crispness.
